projects.title: PDF RAG Chatbot
projects.subtitle: Secure async document intelligence with hybrid retrieval, OCR, abstention, and grounded citations.
highlights: Asynchronous PDF ingestion with worker-based processing and persistent metadata.
Dense, hybrid, and hybrid-rerank retrieval with evidence-based confidence gating and abstention.
Native, scanned, and mixed PDF handling with local OCR plus layout/table-aware extraction.
Validated page citations, retrieval traces, reindex fingerprints, regression evaluation, and security hardening.
projects.architecture: PDF validation → async queue → extraction/OCR → structure-aware chunks → embeddings → Qdrant + lexical retrieval → fusion/reranking → confidence gate → grounded generation → validated citations
projects.caseStudy: Built as an infrastructure-complete RAG backend rather than a chat demo. The system treats ingestion, retrieval quality, confidence calibration, document security, citation validity, and regression testing as first-class engineering problems.
projects.limitations: Evaluation is repository-defined and domain-dependent; OCR and layout heuristics are bounded by configured limits and do not imply universal document understanding.

projects.title: LLM API Gateway
projects.subtitle: Provider-neutral LLM infrastructure with stable aliases, retries, fallback chains, usage accounting, and analytics.
highlights: Stable model aliases decouple application code from provider-specific model names.
Ordered fallback chains, retry/backoff with jitter, gateway timeouts, and normalized errors.
Structured JSON output, embeddings, normalized token usage, cached-token accounting, and cost estimates.
Persistent usage analytics with async tests, routing/fallback coverage, CI, CodeQL, and Dependabot.
projects.architecture: Client → stable alias/router → provider adapter → retry/timeout policy → fallback provider → normalized response + usage ledger
projects.caseStudy: Designed to make provider switching and failure recovery an infrastructure concern instead of leaking vendor-specific behavior into every application.
projects.limitations: Provider behavior and pricing still change externally; the gateway normalizes interfaces but cannot eliminate upstream availability or model-quality differences.

projects.title: Lead Scoring ML API
projects.subtitle: An evaluated supervised-ML inference service with calibration, threshold policy, model integrity checks, and reproducible synthetic benchmarks.
highlights: Deterministic 5,000-row synthetic B2B dataset with explicit non-production benchmark labeling.
Train/validation/test separation, calibration analysis, Brier/log-loss evaluation, and business-cost threshold policy.
Single, batch, and CSV scoring with typed feature contracts and local logistic contribution explanations.
Model manifest and SHA-256 verification before deserialization, CI coverage, CodeQL, and release/container workflows.
projects.architecture: Synthetic dataset → feature pipeline → model selection → calibration + threshold policy → signed artifact manifest → FastAPI inference
projects.caseStudy: The project focuses on the engineering around an ML model: data contracts, probability calibration, decision thresholds, artifact integrity, reproducibility, and honest evaluation boundaries.
projects.limitations: All benchmark metrics are synthetic and must not be interpreted as real CRM performance or causal business impact.

projects.title: AI Engineering Starter Kit
projects.subtitle: A reusable FastAPI foundation for production-minded AI services with typed configuration, persistence, testing, security guardrails, and CI.
highlights: Typed configuration, Gemini integration, structured output, logging, exception handling, and health endpoints.
SQLite/PostgreSQL-ready persistence with SQLAlchemy and Alembic migrations.
Optional API-key authentication plus production guardrails for debug mode, credentials, CORS, and weak keys.
Async tests, mocked provider calls, Ruff, Docker/Compose, CI, Bandit, pip-audit, and migration smoke tests.
projects.architecture: Client → FastAPI routes → service/provider layer → typed schemas → persistence/migrations → observability + tests + CI
projects.caseStudy: A foundation project built to eliminate repeated setup work while keeping production constraints visible from day one.
projects.limitations: It is a starter architecture, not a substitute for application-specific threat modeling, scaling, observability, or domain logic.

projects.title: Wahab Mobiles
projects.subtitle: A production e-commerce platform for a family retail business, spanning storefront, authentication, checkout, administration, and deployment hardening.
highlights: Production-oriented commerce flows for a real family business rather than a portfolio-only demo.
Cookie-based JWT authentication with refresh rotation, role-based administration, and OAuth support.
Server-side checkout recalculation, locking/idempotency, signed guest cart handling, CSRF defenses, rate limits, and security headers.
Containerized deployment topology with API, PostgreSQL, Redis, migrations, and reverse proxy infrastructure.
projects.architecture: React storefront → Fastify API → auth/commerce services → Prisma/PostgreSQL + Redis → containerized reverse-proxy deployment
projects.caseStudy: This project demonstrates full-stack product engineering attached to an operating retail business: customer flows, administrative workflows, data integrity, security controls, and deployment concerns have to work together.
projects.limitations: Commercial details, credentials, operational data, and private business information are intentionally excluded from the public case study.

projects.title: LucidFence
projects.subtitle: A private, self-hosted household network-protection system for DNS filtering, safe-search enforcement, policy controls, and browser-assisted protection.
highlights: Family DNS filtering with safe-search and restricted-mode enforcement plus custom rule management.
Self-hosted local administration, backup/reset workflows, system status, and browser-assisted controls.
Security-focused validation including secret scanning, dependency/container checks, and device/network test planning.
Architecture is public at a high level while source code and operational details remain private during alpha.
projects.architecture: Household devices → DNS/policy layer → filtering + search/video enforcement → local control plane → browser extension + admin workflows
projects.caseStudy: LucidFence explores privacy-preserving family protection as a local systems problem across networking, policy enforcement, web controls, operations, and security—not just as a browser blocklist.
projects.limitations: Private alpha. Physical-device and bypass-resistance testing remains part of the validation process; no production-grade effectiveness claim is made yet.

projects.title: Atlas
projects.subtitle: Procurement intelligence for mapping merchant SKUs to credible upstream sourcing alternatives and comparing evidence-backed acquisition scenarios.
highlights: Maps merchant SKUs to candidate upstream sourcing alternatives using product identity and provenance signals.
Compares acquisition scenarios using landed cost, supplier evidence, and traceable sourcing context.
Designed as a usable product rather than a research-only matching experiment.
Source code is private during development, with open-source release planned after completion.
projects.architecture: Merchant SKU → identity normalization → candidate sourcing discovery → evidence/provenance layer → landed-cost comparison → ranked acquisition scenarios
projects.caseStudy: Atlas is being built around the hard part of procurement intelligence: not merely finding a similar listing, but establishing enough identity, provenance, cost, and supplier evidence to compare sourcing decisions credibly.
projects.limitations: Still under private development. Public usage, benchmark claims, and source release will be added only after validation and launch.

projects.title: MS-ADA Intelligent Traffic Surveillance
projects.subtitle: A CPU-first academic computer-vision prototype for vehicle tracking, ALPR, accident reasoning, hit-and-run monitoring, and evidence capture.
highlights: Real-time vehicle detection and tracking with Pakistani plate recognition and evidence outputs.
Deterministic multi-signal accident reasoning using contact/proximity, relative motion, deceleration, optical flow, and trajectory convergence.
Hit-and-run monitoring, event CSVs, processed video, snapshots/clips, and alert workflows.
Final Year Project at NED University; publication details will be added once the research paper is formally published.
projects.architecture: Video → YOLO detection → persistent tracking → motion/ALPR signals → temporal collision reasoning → evidence capture + alerts
projects.caseStudy: MS-ADA is an academic research prototype that combines computer vision components into an interpretable temporal event pipeline. It is intentionally presented as research rather than as deployment-grade traffic safety infrastructure.
projects.limitations: Academic prototype; no claim of production readiness or universal accident-detection accuracy. Research-paper citation will be added after formal publication.

blog.title: Why My RAG System Learned to Say ‘I Don’t Know’
blog.excerpt: Engineering confidence gates and abstention into retrieval-augmented generation instead of forcing an answer from weak evidence.
blog.content:
# Why my RAG system learned to say ‘I don’t know’

This draft will become an engineering note about retrieval confidence, evidence sufficiency, regression evaluation, and why abstention is a product feature rather than a failure.

## What changed

The system moved from always generating an answer toward explicitly testing whether retrieved evidence was strong enough to justify generation.

## What I would measure

- Retrieval quality
- Answer support
- Citation validity
- False-confidence rate

This post is intentionally kept as a draft until the final case-study evidence and examples are ready.
